title: Remove Trailing Zeros From a String
statement: The string `num` holds the decimal digits of a positive integer, written without leading zeros. Delete every `'0'` at the end of `num` (all the zeros that come after its last non-zero digit) and return the remaining string. If `num` does not end in `'0'`, return it unchanged.
notes:
## Intuition

The answer is a prefix of `num`: everything up to and including its last non-zero digit. So walk backwards from the end, skipping zeros, and cut the string at the first non-zero digit you meet. Because `num` is a positive number with no leading zeros, its first digit is non-zero, so the walk always stops before running off the front.

## Approach

1. Set `end` to `num.length`: the prefix to keep is `num[0..end)`.
2. While the last kept digit `num[end - 1]` is `'0'`, shrink the prefix by decreasing `end`.
3. Return `num.slice(0, end)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`num = "51230100"`, length 8:

- `end = 8`: `num[7]` is `'0'`, so `end` becomes 7.
- `end = 7`: `num[6]` is `'0'`, so `end` becomes 6.
- `end = 6`: `num[5]` is `'1'`, so the loop stops.

The kept prefix `num.slice(0, 6)` is `"512301"`. The zero inside it, at index 4, stays because it is not at the end.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each trailing zero is visited once, then one slice copies the prefix.
- Space: O(n) for the returned string.

## Pitfalls

- Only zeros at the very end are removed; zeros in the middle, as in `"505050"`, must stay.
- Do not convert `num` to a number: it can have up to 1000 digits, far beyond what `Number` stores exactly.
- If you work on a string that might be all zeros, add an `end > 0` guard; here the guarantee of no leading zeros makes it unnecessary.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `end` | length of the prefix being kept; `num[end - 1]` is its last digit |

narration.1: num stays a string throughout: with up to 1000 digits it is far too long for a number type.
narration.2: Start by keeping the whole string; end is the length of the prefix to return.
narration.4: Look at the last digit still kept: is it a zero?
narration.5: Yes: drop it by shrinking the kept prefix by one.
narration.7: The last kept digit is non-zero, so return everything before end.
